title: Local thermal flags missed more large total steric rises in the Atlantic than the Pacific in NOAA upper-700-m fields at 60 S-60 N in 2016-2025
abstract: We tested whether a local thermal upper-tail flag marks large total steric rises equally well in the Atlantic and Pacific. We used NOAA upper-700-m seasonal fields, annual changes, and twelve equally weighted latitude bands at 60 S-60 N. Separate local 90th-percentile thermal and total thresholds used 2006-2015 changes. The test used 2016-2025 changes. Thermal flags missed 43.4% of total flags in the Atlantic and 31.0% in the Pacific. The Atlantic-minus-Pacific difference was 12.45 percentage points, with conditional 95% three-year block limits of 6.83 to 17.31 points. Its sign held with other block lengths, 80th and 95th percentiles, natural area weights and reversed decades. The Pacific miss rate was higher in the two northernmost bands. A thermal flag remained informative but did not mark all large total steric rises. This tests an indicator for the same time, not a forecast or coastal flood risk. One mapped product, ten test years, overlapping annual pairs and intervals conditional on fixed thresholds limit inference. The package gives new code, aggregate evidence, paired draws, source hashes, source and aggregate audits, and reproduction instructions. Raw NOAA grids stay external.
